facts.value: Maintain a healthy weight by eating roughly the same number of calories that your body is using.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Limit intake of fats to no more than 30% of total caloric intake, preferring unsaturated fats to saturated fats. Avoid trans fats.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Eat at least 400 grams of fruits and vegetables per day (not counting potatoes, sweet potatoes, cassava, and other starchy roots). A healthy diet also contains legumes (e.g. lentils, beans), whole grains, and nuts.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Limit the intake of simple sugars to less than 10% of caloric intake (below 5% of calories or 25 grams may be even better).
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Limit salt from all sources and ensure that salt is iodized. Less than 5 grams of salt per day can reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Ensure that the foods chosen have sufficient vitamins and certain minerals.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Avoid directly poisonous (e.g. heavy metals) and carcinogenic (e.g. benzene) substances.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Avoid foods contaminated by human pathogens (e.g. E. coli, tapeworm eggs).
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Replace saturated fats with polyunsaturated fats in the diet, which can reduce the risk of coronary artery disease and diabetes.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree

facts.value: Insufficient vegetables and fruit is the cause of 2.8% of deaths worldwide.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree
